The drawer is where skills get applied and guardrails added/removed. Build it for Content Engine (generate + plan) and Agent Kanban (plan + build), the two modules he runs most. Two halves. (1) STOP: extend moduleRuns with an AbortController per run (ctx.signal) and a stopModuleRun(id) that aborts it and marks status 'stopped' with who/when; expose POST /api/runs/:id {action:'stop'}; pass ctx.signal into cliComplete / multiModelComplete so the child CLI actually dies (loopEngine already supports signal; check contentEngine.multiModelComplete and the kanban routes and thread the signal through); RunsTray shows a STOP button on running runs. The route receives the chosen values in the POST body and honors them; unknown fields are rejected, not ignored. Wire Content Engine first, then Kanban; keep Deal Desk untouched (S4 owns it). features.description: Owner spec (bug list): the WebMCP builder should be a wizard, not an input page. Step 1: the user gives an exact description of what the tool should do (vague or granular). Step 2: an AI digests it, asks clarifying questions, and reasons in a scratchpad WITHOUT writing code: a proposed tool list (name, one-job purpose, inputs, persona/category). Step 3: the user approves or edits the list. Step 4: only then the agent emits the JSON spec following the existing exporter's schema and best practices: 5-10 tools per server, one tool one job, unused tools cut, tools split by persona or category. Escape hatch: a 'write your own JSON' mode where the agent only proofreads and reports problems. Build it as a stepper inside the existing /webmcp builder with server-side routes for digest (questions + proposal), and emit; the model call goes through the existing cliComplete/provider seam and honours the selected provider (never a silent fallback). Persist wizard drafts so a refresh does not lose the conversation. Smokes: the proposal->JSON transform with a mocked model, schema validation of emitted specs, the proofread path flagging a bad spec.
acceptance_criteria: The /webmcp builder offers Wizard and Write-my-own modes; the wizard has description -> clarify/propose -> approve -> emit steps and never emits JSON before approval.
Emitted specs validate against the existing WebMCP schema and respect 5-10 tools, one job per tool, persona/category split.
